# Environment and secret inventory

Every secret this system holds, what it controls, where it lives and how it is rotated. Read by scripts/check-secret-rotation.mjs, which refuses a secret-shaped environment variable the code reads and this file does not classify, an entry whose rotation procedure is not a real heading in docs/runbooks/key-rotation.md, and a key-encrypting key with no retired slot to keep the outgoing version in. It is the companion to build/secret-allowlist.json: that file answers 'is a credential committed', this one answers 'when this one leaks, what does somebody do about it at 02:00'. No value is ever stored here — only names, owners and procedures.

Generated from `build/secret-inventory.json`. `pnpm rotation` holds it against the secret-shaped
names the code reads; `pnpm processors` holds it against the keys `packages/config/src/env.ts`
declares, in both directions. Adding a credential therefore fails the build until its rotation is
written down, which is the only moment the person who knows how it works is still looking at it.

## Where each one lives

### `CLINICAL_KEK`

The deployment secret store, injected as an environment variable. Never in the database: clinical.kek_version holds version labels only.

Rotation slots: `CLINICAL_KEK_VERSION` (version label), `CLINICAL_KEK_PREVIOUS` (retired key), `CLINICAL_KEK_PREVIOUS_VERSION` (retired version label).

Rotation re-wraps data keys and rewrites no ciphertext, so it runs against a live database. Exercised against synthetic fixtures only until OPEN-QUESTIONS Y5-residency is answered and real intake data may be loaded.

### `GOOGLE_TOKEN_KEK`

The deployment secret store, injected as an environment variable. public.google_connection.refresh_token_kid holds the version label only.

Rotation slots: `GOOGLE_TOKEN_KEK_VERSION` (version label), `GOOGLE_TOKEN_KEK_PREVIOUS` (retired key), `GOOGLE_TOKEN_KEK_PREVIOUS_VERSION` (retired version label).

A separate key from the clinical one deliberately. packages/google/src/rewrap.ts performs the re-wrap and has no caller yet, so this rotation is procedural rather than scripted — see the NOTE on H-HARD-03 in build/manifest.yaml.

### `STAFF_PII_KEK`

The deployment secret store, injected as an environment variable. Never in the database: employee_bank_detail.detail_kid and employee_document.number_kid hold version labels only, and there is deliberately no version registry table yet (migration 0050 says why).

Rotation slots: `STAFF_PII_KEK_VERSION` (version label), `STAFF_PII_KEK_PREVIOUS` (retired key), `STAFF_PII_KEK_PREVIOUS_VERSION` (retired version label).

A third key, separate from the clinical one deliberately: an employment record does not relocate with the clinical store (ADR 0010), so one key would either strand this estate at relocation or exist in two places. packages/hr/src/staff-secret.ts performs the per-row re-wrap and has no caller, so this rotation is a runbook procedure rather than a command - the same position packages/google/src/rewrap.ts is in, and for the same reason recorded there.

### `DATABASE_URL`

The deployment secret store. The password half is also in the DigitalOcean control panel, which is where it is changed.

**If it is wrong or missing:** A managed-database password change is immediate and drops every open connection; the application reconnects with the new URL only after it is redeployed, so there is a gap of one deploy. Do it outside trading hours (11:00 to 02:00, Asia/Dubai).

### `PAYLOAD_SECRET`

The deployment secret store.

**If it is wrong or missing:** Every admin session and every unused password-reset link is invalidated the moment it changes. Nobody is locked out permanently, but everybody signs in again, so it is announced rather than done quietly.

### `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`

The deployment secret store, and the Google Cloud console, which is where it is rotated.

Google allows two client secrets on one client at once, so the new one is added, deployed, and the old one deleted afterwards. Stored refresh tokens survive: they are bound to the client id, not the secret.

### `SENTRY_DSN`

The deployment secret store.

### `—`

public.google_connection.refresh_token_ct, sealed under GOOGLE_TOKEN_KEK. Never in an environment variable and never in a log; scripts/check-google-token-chokepoint.mjs enforces where it may be named at all.

**If it is wrong or missing:** Rotating the token itself needs the owner to re-consent in a browser, and the connection reports needs_reauth until they do. Rotating the KEK that wraps it does not — that is a re-wrap, and it is the reason refresh_token_kid exists.

### `DOCUMENT_URL_SIGNING_SECRET`

The deployment secret store, injected as an environment variable. Never in the database: private_document_fetch.signature_key_version holds a version LABEL only, and a signing key stored beside the log of what it signed would defeat the one thing the detached signature buys - that a database dump cannot mint a link.

Rotation slots: `DOCUMENT_URL_SIGNING_SECRET_VERSION` (version label), `DOCUMENT_URL_SIGNING_SECRET_PREVIOUS` (retired key), `DOCUMENT_URL_SIGNING_SECRET_PREVIOUS_VERSION` (retired version label).

Classified signing-key and not kek: nothing is encrypted with it, so no document becomes unreadable if it is lost - every link simply stops opening and a reader mints a new one. Zero-downtime BECAUSE of the retired slot, and that slot is the interesting half. Links live fifteen minutes (DOCUMENT_SIGNATURE_TTL_SECONDS), so without it a rotation would kill every link minted in the previous fifteen minutes and the holder would see a document that will not open with nothing to distinguish that from a refusal. Verification consults both keys and signing only ever uses the current one, so the rotation is a one-way door rather than a state where two keys are both current; DOCUMENT_URL_SIGNING_SECRET_PREVIOUS may be dropped once one TTL has elapsed, unlike the suppression pepper's, which is retained indefinitely.

### `SUPPRESSION_PEPPER`

The deployment secret store, injected as an environment variable. Never in the database: suppression.pepper_version holds a version label only, and a pepper stored beside the digests it peppers adds nothing against the one attack it exists to answer - a database dump.

Rotation slots: `SUPPRESSION_PEPPER_VERSION` (version label), `SUPPRESSION_PEPPER_PREVIOUS` (retired key), `SUPPRESSION_PEPPER_PREVIOUS_VERSION` (retired version label).

Classified signing-key and not kek: nothing is encrypted with it, so no record becomes unreadable if it is lost. The retired slot is declared anyway and is the important half - reads consult both peppers, so the rotation itself is seamless, but a row whose plaintext recipient this system no longer holds can never be re-keyed (customer has no email column at all, C-CRM-01 NOTE 3), so SUPPRESSION_PEPPER_PREVIOUS is retained indefinitely rather than until a sweep finishes. Deleting it turns those rows into rows nothing will ever match, which presents as a promotional message to somebody who opted out. The runbook states this under its own heading.

### `PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET`

The deployment secret store, injected as an environment variable. Never in the database: it is the gateway's half of a shared secret, and a copy beside the rows it authenticates would be readable by anything that can read those rows.

**If it is wrong or missing:** Webhook delivery only, and only if the chosen gateway cannot hold two secrets active at once. Nothing a customer touches stops: a booking, a payment authorisation and the till do not read this secret. An unverifiable delivery answers 503, which a gateway retries, so the window costs delay rather than events - and Y-PAY-05's reconciliation pass is the check that says none was lost. The length of the window is the gateway's retry ladder, which is unknown until one is chosen (Y7-gateway).

No gateway is chosen (Y7-gateway), so there is no secret in any environment yet and 365 days is this repository's own floor for a shared secret with no regulatory period, the same figure database-url and google-refresh-token carry; it is a schedule, not a measurement, and the overlap window a rotation needs is the chosen gateway's. `zeroDowntime` is false for the same reason: whether two secrets can be active at once is the gateway's answer. Absent, the endpoint answers 503 and the gateway retries; it never answers 401, which would make it abandon a valid event. Added by the integrator at the final verify, where `pnpm rotation` refused the undeclared variable Y-PAY-04 introduced.

## Deliberately not secrets

Each of these is an environment variable something reads and this inventory classifies as not
needing a rotation procedure. The reason is recorded rather than implied, because "it is not a
secret" is the sentence somebody writes about a key that turns out to be one.

- **`TEST_DATABASE_URL`** — Non-production only, and the credential in it is the documented loopback development one. scripts/check-secrets.mjs exempts loopback hosts structurally for the same reason: a database nobody outside the machine can reach is not a secret. A value here pointing anywhere but loopback is a misconfiguration, not a rotation.
- **`ZOHO_TOKEN`** — NOT A CREDENTIAL THIS SYSTEM HOLDS, AND THE POINT IS THAT IT CANNOT BECOME ONE. The name appears in exactly one place: gate case 130v in scripts/test-gates.mjs, which temporarily edits packages/db/src/services/zoho-export.ts to read it and requires two checks to reject the result — pnpm no-autofile for the credential read, and zoho-export.itest.ts, which runs the export with process.env emptied. ADR 0052: the Zoho Books export is bytes handed to a person, so there is nothing to authenticate to and nowhere for a token to arrive, and an export that needed one would fail the build. There is therefore no rotation procedure to declare, because there is no value. If this name ever appears outside that gate case, the entry is wrong and the gate is what will say so.
- **`APP_ENV`** — Which environment this is: one of five declared names, and the only required key in packages/config/src/env.ts that carries no credential and reaches no provider. It is in this list rather than absent because H-HARD-09's check holds this inventory against the config schema in both directions, and "required by the schema" is the rule acceptance line 4 states, so a required key has to be either classified or explicitly not a secret, with a reason. Knowing the value tells somebody nothing they could not read off the hostname, and it is the one key whose absence is caught loudly at boot rather than quietly at 01:00.
- **`DATABASE_CA_CERT`** — A certificate authority's PUBLIC certificate, which is published by construction — DigitalOcean prints it with `doctl databases ca`, and every client that verifies a connection to the cluster already holds it. Nothing about it is confidential and there is nothing to rotate on a schedule: it changes when the provider rotates its CA, which is an availability event rather than a security one. It is in packages/config/src/env.ts because the alternative is an ambient process.env read in the one place that needs it, and it is here because a name that looks credential-shaped and is not should say so explicitly rather than be absent from both lists.
